intro_html: Bacon, butter and mushrooms build the base. Wild rice gives it that nutty chew, turkey breast gives it the muscle, and a splash of cream at the end pulls it all together. This is a cold weather soup that eats like a full plate of food, and a squeeze of lemon at the finish keeps the whole rich thing from sitting too heavy.
cost_closing_html: About $3.48 a bowl. That is the top of our range, and the wild rice is why. If you want this closer to the middle of the pack, that is the line to look at first.
shop_smart: Wild rice is the expensive ingredient, not the turkey. Check the bulk bins and the warehouse club before the boxed brands. If it is out of reach that week, a long grain brown rice will carry the soup at a fraction of the price.
Buy whole white mushrooms and slice them yourself. Pre-sliced costs more per ounce and goes slimy days sooner.
Bacon is a seasoning here, not a main. Buy a pound, use what the recipe calls for, and freeze the rest in flat portions for the next few batches.
The flour and butter roux replaces store-bought thickener. Pennies of flour do the job that a can of condensed soup charges you a couple dollars for.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the wild rice separately per the package until tender and set it aside. It takes longer than white rice, so start it first.
Chop the bacon and render it in your big pot with the olive oil until crisp, then lift the bacon out and leave the fat behind.
Add the butter, then the diced onion, celery and carrots, and cook until soft. Add the sliced mushrooms and cook until they give up their water and start to brown.
Stir in the garlic, the dried thyme and the Italian seasoning, then sprinkle the flour over everything and stir for two minutes to cook out the raw taste.
Pour in the chicken broth slowly while stirring so the roux does not lump, then simmer until it thickens.
Add the cooked wild rice, the turkey breast and the heavy cream, warm it through without boiling, then finish with the lemon juice, the reserved bacon, salt and black pepper.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1. Divide by 14 and ladle that exact weight into each container. Every bowl lands near 697 calories with 38 grams of protein, so this one is a serious dinner. It thickens overnight, so thin it with a splash of broth when you reheat.
upsell_html: A creamy, bacon-backed turkey soup for about $3.48 a bowl. This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

head.description: Wild rice, mushrooms, bacon and turkey breast in a creamy thyme broth. A hearty 14 serving soup portioned by weight for meal prep.
head.keywords: creamy turkey wild rice soup, mushroom soup recipe, leftover turkey soup, budget meal prep, wild rice soup, cheap dinner
steps: Cook the wild rice separately until tender and set aside.
Render the bacon in the pot, remove it, and cook the onion, celery, carrots and mushrooms in the fat and butter.
Stir in the garlic and herbs, dust with flour, and cook two minutes.
Whisk in the chicken broth and simmer until thickened.
Add the wild rice, turkey breast and cream, warm through, and finish with lemon juice and the bacon.
